doc.title: Mrs. P. Thomas Agnes Brown Interview, 1960-10-12

title: Hearing Tom at Audubon Park; who really started jazz
summary: The interviewer first heard Tom with Red Hot Bergen; they discuss the original band with Larry Shields replacing Gussie, arguments over who originated jazz, and Tom's father's band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: He plays in St. Lafonses' Arden on Sunday. Right there. You know where I first heard Tom was up uh Audubon Park with uh Red Hot Bergen. Oh yeah. And that was a good band there. Oh yes. With Harry Shields on clarinet. I know.
Billy Bergen. Red Hot we call them.
And let's see over here you have the original band you say. Yeah. Except that Larry Shields was taking Gussie's place. That's right. Correct.
So. So like Gussie said Larry, he's gone two weeks now. He said if they could get down to the root of jazz. Get it straightened out.

They haven't got the root. No it's it's going to be awful hard because so many people tell you different stories. Sure. I know. Well everybody knows that uh certainly Tom thought up a lot of the licks and everything.

You know uh some man told me not long ago they get in arguments in Barons and they fight over Tom. This guy says he wasn't and he says sure I'm sure Tom was the right one. They have arguments. That's funny. Oh. It's ridiculous. Well. Ridiculous is right.
Everybody knows that Tom was playing long before the the people that claimed to have been in it.
Tom was playing before them. You see uh Tom's father was a Browns band too. I've heard that. His father. I guess he taught the boys you know.

And you've got a lot of sheet music around. Oh. I guess some of this belongs to Tom too. All of that's yes. See a fool in love. Till then. Till then. Blue. Blue. Yeah. By uh Grant Clark, Edgar Leslie and Lou Handelman.
